title: Washtub bass
summary: A washtub bass is built from an upturned metal tub, a broomstick and a length of cord. The stick stands on the rim, the cord runs from its top to the tub, and a pluck on the stretched cord gives a deep bass note that the tub makes boom.
howToPlay: Five places are lit: four places along the cord, from Low to High, and the Slap on the tub itself.
Pluck the place a closing ring marks. The cord trembles and the tub rings.
The slap is a short knock between the bass notes, so keep it light.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A bass made from a tub, a pole and a rope costs almost nothing, so it filled out jug bands and skiffle groups where no one could buy a double bass.
credits: Tradition: the washtub bass; patterns written for this game
